key_insight: The paper argues that current world models are judged mostly by how well they generate realistic observations, but not by whether they maintain a persistent internal state that continues evolving when unobserved. In simple terms: they can paint the scene, but may not actually 'remember' and update the world behind the scenes.
problem_solved: It addresses the evaluation gap in world-model benchmarks: existing tests often miss whether a model can represent durable objects, ongoing events, and hidden state over time without relying on immediate visual input.
method: Identifies the missing 'persistent state core' as a key capability for world models.
Frames evaluation around state continuity and evolution, not just frame-by-frame visual realism.
Highlights why benchmark design must test whether internal world state persists and updates even when observations are absent.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shifts attention from video quality to stateful reasoning and long-horizon consistency. It suggests better benchmarks for building agents and simulators that can support planning, prediction, and real-world interaction.

paper_title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
